description: Running production services reliably at scale: reliability goals expressed as service level indicators, objectives and error budgets, monitoring and alerting, incident response and blameless postmortems, capacity planning, load balancing and failover, and automation that removes toil. Practised through simulated outages, on-call rotations and failover drills in browser-based consoles and terminals, taught to the depth of a strong final-year reliability engineering course.
modelledOn: Beyer, Jones, Petoff and Murphy, Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems
Beyer, Murphy, Rensin, Kawahara and Thorne, The Site Reliability Workbook
Nygard, Release It! Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software
Allspaw, The Art of Capacity Planning
outcomes: Define service level indicators and objectives that reflect user experience and manage releases with error budgets.
Design monitoring and alerting that pages humans only for urgent, actionable, user-visible problems.
Lead and take part in incident response using clear roles, communication and mitigation-first practices.
Write blameless postmortems that identify contributing factors and drive lasting improvements.
Forecast demand, plan capacity and design load balancing, redundancy and failover for target availability.
Measure and reduce toil through automation, safe release engineering and controlled chaos experiments.

units.title: Reliability goals and error budgets
topics: What SRE is: software engineering applied to operations; how it relates to DevOps and traditional operations
Availability, latency, durability and correctness; the cost of each additional nine
Service level indicators, objectives and agreements; choosing SLIs from user journeys
Error budgets and error budget policies; balancing feature velocity against reliability
SLOs for a mobile money transfer service and a national exam results portal on release day

units.title: Monitoring and alerting
topics: White-box and black-box monitoring; the four golden signals; the USE and RED methods
Metrics, logs and traces; time series, labels and cardinality; Prometheus and Grafana
Alerting on symptoms not causes; burn-rate alerts on SLOs; reducing alert fatigue
Synthetic probes and real user monitoring; monitoring from networks in different African countries
Dashboards that answer questions; runbooks linked from every alert

units.title: Incident response
topics: On-call: rotations, handovers, escalation policies, sustainable load and compensation
Incident command: incident commander, operations lead, communications lead, scribe
Mitigate first: rollbacks, feature flags, traffic draining, graceful degradation
Communication during incidents: status pages, stakeholder updates, customer messages
Simulated incidents: a database failover, a bad deploy and an upstream payment provider outage

units.title: Postmortems
topics: Blameless culture and why blame hides information
Writing a postmortem: timeline, impact, detection, response, contributing factors, action items
Analysis techniques: five whys and its limits, causal diagrams, systems thinking about complex failures
Tracking action items to completion; learning from public postmortems of major outages

units.title: Capacity planning
topics: Demand forecasting: organic growth, seasonality, events such as month-end salaries and festive seasons
Load testing and finding the saturation point; queueing theory basics and Little's law
Headroom, N+1 and N+2 redundancy; provisioning lead times for cloud and on-premises hardware
Autoscaling policies and their failure modes; cost as a capacity constraint
Planning around unreliable power and connectivity: generators, UPS, multiple internet providers

units.title: Load balancing and failover
topics: Layer 4 and layer 7 load balancing; algorithms: round robin, least connections, consistent hashing
Health checks, connection draining, overload protection, load shedding and rate limiting
Resilience patterns: timeouts, retries with jitter, circuit breakers, bulkheads; cascading failures
DNS and global load balancing; active-active and active-passive multi-region designs
Database replication and failover; recovery time and recovery point objectives; disaster recovery drills

units.title: Automation and toil reduction
topics: Defining and measuring toil; the toil budget
Automation maturity: from runbooks to scripts to self-healing systems; when not to automate
Release engineering: CI/CD, canary releases, progressive delivery, automated rollback
Configuration as code and infrastructure as code as reliability tools

units.title: Reliability practice and capstone
topics: Chaos engineering: hypotheses, blast radius, game days
Production readiness reviews and launch checklists
Organising SRE: embedded, centralised and consulting models; reliability in small teams
Capstone: define SLOs, build monitoring, run an incident drill and write the postmortem for a simulated service

schedule.title: SRE, availability and SLOs
schedule.exercise: Short problem set: convert availability targets to allowed downtime per month and choose three SLIs for a mobile money transfer service.

tasks.title: Compute and compare monthly downtime allowed by 99, 99.9 and 99.99 percent availability for a simulated service and note the cost of each
Define SLIs for success rate and latency of a transfer service from its user journey and measure them over a simulated day
Decide which of six operational tasks belong to an SRE role rather than traditional operations or development, and justify each on a rubric

schedule.title: Error budgets and release policy
schedule.exercise: Write an error budget policy for an exam results portal, stating what happens when the budget is spent.

tasks.title: Calculate the remaining error budget of a service after a simulated outage and decide whether a release can proceed
Resolve a conflict between a product manager who wants a launch and an SRE with a burned error budget, scored on policy and evidence
Set SLOs and an error budget for a national exam results portal and show how they would hold under a ten-times traffic spike on release day

schedule.title: Monitoring and alerting
schedule.exercise: Choose golden signals for three services and write one symptom-based alert and one burn-rate alert for each.

tasks.title: Identify the four golden signals for a web service from its dashboard and mark which one is failing in a given incident
Instrument a service with request counters and latency histograms and build a dashboard of rate, errors and duration
Replace ten noisy cause-based alerts with two burn-rate alerts on an SLO and show fewer false pages in a replay of last month

schedule.title: Probes, dashboards and runbooks
schedule.exercise: Write a runbook for the alert 'transfer error rate high', including diagnosis steps and rollback options.

tasks.title: Configure a synthetic probe against a service endpoint and read the probe results to decide whether the service is up
Build a dashboard that answers whether users are affected, which component is failing and what changed, and link a runbook to each alert
Compare probes from three vantage points with real user data from different countries to find an outage visible only in one region

schedule.title: On-call and incident command
schedule.exercise: Draft an on-call rotation and escalation policy for a team of five, with limits on night pages.

tasks.title: Design an on-call rotation for five engineers and a handover note, scoring fairness, coverage and sustainability against a rubric
Lead a simulated incident as incident commander, assigning operations, communications and scribe roles and choosing between actions as new evidence arrives
Mitigate a failing deploy by rolling back, turning off a feature flag and draining traffic, and choose the fastest safe action under time pressure

schedule.title: Communication and incident drills
schedule.exercise: Write three status page updates for a payment provider outage at different stages of the incident.

tasks.title: Write a status update and a customer message for an outage at 20, 60 and 120 minutes, choosing what to say with the evidence you have
Respond to a database primary failure by promoting a replica, checking for data loss and restoring traffic within a 15-minute target
Handle a bad deploy and an upstream payment provider outage at the same time by degrading features gracefully and report the user impact

schedule.title: Blameless postmortems
schedule.exercise: Rewrite a blame-heavy incident report as a blameless postmortem with timeline, impact, contributing factors and action items.

tasks.title: Identify blaming language in an incident report and rewrite it so the system and process causes are the focus, scored on a rubric
Write a postmortem with timeline, impact, detection time, response and action items from the raw evidence of a simulated outage
Analyse a complex outage with five whys and a causal diagram, show where five whys alone misses an interacting cause and propose fixes

schedule.title: Capacity planning
schedule.exercise: Forecast traffic for a month-end salary peak and decide how many servers the service needs with a safety margin.

tasks.title: Forecast next month's requests from a growth trend and a month-end peak and set a target number of instances
Load test a service step by step to find the saturation point and apply Little's law to the observed queue and latency figures
Provision an N+2 design with headroom for a festive season peak, given a two-week lead time on hardware, and justify its cost

schedule.title: Autoscaling and unreliable infrastructure
schedule.exercise: Write a plan for keeping a Kumasi office service up through power cuts and one internet provider failure.

tasks.title: Configure an autoscaling policy on CPU and observe how it responds to a traffic ramp, noting the scale-up delay
Find the failure modes of an autoscaling policy that oscillates or scales too late, fix it and compare cost and latency
Plan power and connectivity redundancy for a branch office with generators, UPS and two internet providers, scoring cost against availability targets

schedule.title: Load balancing and resilience patterns
schedule.exercise: Explain, with a diagram, how retries without jitter turn a small failure into a cascading outage.

tasks.title: Configure a load balancer with round robin and least connections and compare how each spreads uneven requests over three servers
Add health checks, connection draining and a rate limit to a load balancer and show a failing server is removed without dropping requests
Break a service with a retry storm, then add timeouts, jittered retries and a circuit breaker and show it recovers

schedule.title: Global load balancing and disaster recovery
schedule.exercise: Write a disaster recovery plan with RTO and RPO targets for a service with a primary database.

tasks.title: Configure DNS-based failover between two regions and fail the primary region to watch traffic switch
Fail over a replicated database, measure the data lost and recovery time, and compare with the stated RPO and RTO
Run a disaster recovery drill for a two-region service, find the gaps in the plan and rewrite it to meet a 30-minute RTO

schedule.title: Toil, automation and release engineering
schedule.exercise: Measure toil in a week of an on-call log and propose three automations ranked by time saved against effort.

tasks.title: Count repetitive manual tasks in a sample terminal session and compute the share of the week that is toil
Release a change with a canary to 5 percent of traffic, watch the metrics and roll back automatically when errors exceed a threshold
Write a script that provisions and configures a server from code, rerun it to show it is idempotent and detect a manual configuration drift

schedule.title: Chaos, readiness and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone deliverable: SLO document, monitoring plan, incident drill log and postmortem for a simulated service.

tasks.title: Run a game day that kills one server and adds latency to a dependency, comparing the outcome to a hypothesis you wrote beforehand
Review a service launch against a production readiness checklist, find the missing items and decide whether to approve the launch
Define SLOs, build monitoring, run an incident drill and write a postmortem for a simulated service, meeting an availability target
